description: Use case: the inheritance split of a securities depot into the parent portfolio and two child portfolios, respecting the lot sizes, as shown on the page 'Portfolio Split Calculator' (src/test/resources/web/html/use_cases/portfolio_split_calculator_sample.html). The inputs are the holdings, prices, lot sizes and exchange rates of the synthetic bank report (portfolio_report.json), the instruments and their issuers (portfolio_instruments.json) and the 30 / 35 / 35 split agreement with the agreed allocation of the two Lindt & Sprüngli holdings (portfolio_split_parameters_sample.json). The holdings are walked from the largest unit value times lot size to the smallest: the first child gets its target share of the holding value minus the deviation carried in from the holdings before, rounded to the lot size; the second child gets the same count, because both target shares are equal; the parent keeps the remainder, so every holding is conserved exactly; and the cash at the end, divisible to 0.01, closes the remaining drift to below one centime. The holding values, the remainder of the parent, the target values and the final split deviation are formulas of this file reproduced by the calc-validation; the rounding to the lot size and the carried deviation need a round function and a walk in a fixed order, so the allocations of the two children and the cumulative deviation after each step are stored as modelled values of the walk.

triples.name: exchange rate
triples.description: An exchange rate is the rate at which one currency will be exchanged for another. It is also regarded as the value of one country's currency in relation to another currency.

triples.name: ranking number
triples.description: an ordinal position in a ranking (first, second, third, ...), used to disambiguate words like 'second' that also are a time unit

triples.name: second (ranking)
triples.description: the ranking-number reading of the ambiguous word 'second'; displayed as 'second' with 'ranking number' shown only in the tooltip

triples.name: bond (finance)
triples.description: the finance reading of the ambiguous word 'bond': a debt security under which the issuer owes the holders the face value and the interest

triples.name: parent portfolio
triples.description: the part of the original portfolio that the parent keeps, the remainder of every holding

triples.name: first child portfolio
triples.description: the part of the original portfolio that the first child receives

triples.name: second child portfolio
triples.description: the part of the original portfolio that the second child receives

triples.name: portfolio split
triples.description: the division of a securities depot into the portfolios of several beneficiaries, e.g. of an inheritance, respecting the lot sizes

triples.name: example portfolio split
triples.description: the default split of the page 'Portfolio Split Calculator': the depot of the sample bank report split into the parent portfolio (30 percent) and two child portfolios (35 percent each); the holdings are walked from the largest lot value to the smallest, the first child gets the rounded share of its target minus the deviation carried in, the second child the same count, the parent the remainder, and the cash at the end absorbs what is left

triples.name: bond price
triples.description: the price of a bond in percent of its face value

triples.name: face value
triples.description: the nominal amount of a bond on which the interest is paid and which is repaid at maturity

triples.name: holding value
triples.description: the market value of one holding in CHF: the shares times the stock price, the face value times the bond price, or the cash amount times the exchange rate

triples.name: target share
triples.description: the agreed share of the portfolio value that a beneficiary should receive

triples.name: target value
triples.description: the portfolio value times the target share of a beneficiary

triples.name: realised value
triples.description: the sum of the holding values that a beneficiary receives after the rounding

triples.name: cumulative deviation
triples.description: the realised value minus the plain weighted value over all holdings split so far; subtracted once from the target of the next holding

triples.name: split deviation
triples.description: the realised value minus the target value of a beneficiary after the whole walk

formulas.name: stock holding value
formulas.description: the market value of a stock holding: the shares times the stock price

formulas.name: bond holding value
formulas.description: the market value of a bond holding in its own currency: the face value times the bond price in percent of the face value

formulas.name: foreign bond holding value
formulas.description: the market value in CHF of a bond in another currency: the face value times the bond price times the exchange rate

formulas.name: foreign cash holding value
formulas.description: the value in CHF of a cash holding in another currency: the amount times the exchange rate

formulas.name: parent remainder
formulas.description: the parent keeps what is left of a holding after both children have been served, so that every original holding is conserved exactly

formulas.name: target value of a beneficiary
formulas.description: the CHF amount a beneficiary should receive: the portfolio value times the agreed target share

formulas.name: split deviation formula
formulas.description: how much a beneficiary receives more or less than the target after the rounding to the lot sizes
